note.question: How does acquisition uncertainty affect sequential search?
note.overview: This paper studies a variation of the classical Pandora’s problem in which a decision maker (DM) sequentially explores alternatives from a given set and learns their values while trying to acquire the best alternative. The variations in the model we study are (i) alternatives randomly become unavailable during exploration and (ii) the DM’s ability to acquire a remaining alternative is uncertain and depends on a chosen offer price. The paper's central insight is that despite the complexity that these acquisition uncertainties create, simple greedy policies based on static sequencing and a single threshold value enjoy strong performance guarantees.
